title: Space: count the safe squares, then look for the lever
outcomes: Counts the squares each side's pawns attack in the other side's half and says who has more pawn space (the app's count)
Finds the piece with the fewest safe squares (squares no enemy pawn attacks) and tells it from a piece blocked by its own men
Checks whether an enemy pawn can attack the pawns that give the space before trusting a space edge
Tells a position with no pawn space to count from one with a space edge

steps.text: In this app, **space** is counted from pawns only: the squares in the opponent's half of the board that your pawns attack. A white pawn on e5 attacks d6 and f6, so enemy pieces cannot use those squares without risk. A square is safe for a piece when no enemy pawn attacks it. More such squares usually leaves the other side's pieces fewer places to go. It is a count, not a judgement: it does not say the space is useful.

steps.caption: Black to move. White's pawns attack 6 squares in Black's half (b5, c5, d5, d6, e5, f6); Black's pawns attack 0. Count White's pawn squares first. Then look at Black's bishop on b6: one of its squares, c5, is attacked by White's d4 pawn.

line.say: Bc5 steps onto a square White's d4 pawn attacks, so the pawn can simply capture it. A space pawn takes squares away from enemy pieces.
dxc5: the pawn takes the bishop.

claims.statement: White's pawns attack 6 square(s) in the opponent's half: b5, c5, d5, d6, e5 and f6.
Black's pawns attack 0 square(s) in the opponent's half: none.
The black bishop on b6 attacks c5.
The white pawn on e5 attacks d6 and f6.
Exactly one white pawn (d4) attacks c5.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** A space edge helps most when the other side's pieces really have few safe squares and no pawn can attack your space pawns. If a pawn can, the cramped side may free itself with that lever. Count the squares first, then ask: what can the other side attack with one pawn move? The next three positions differ in one feature.

steps.title: Same space, a different lever
steps.prompt: Predict, then check. The second position moves one Black pawn; in the third the two White space pawns are gone.
In a new position, how sure are you that you can tell whether a space edge is real? Write the first two things you would check.
